item.title: Flashpoint Archive – Over 200k web games and animations preserved
item.description:
Welcome Flashpoint Archive is a community effort to preserve games and animations from the web. This project is dedicated to preserving as many experiences from these platforms as possible, so that they aren't lost to time. Among the software that powers Flashpoint is a fully-featured launcher that acts as a frontend for the collection, a proxy that tricks games into thinking they're running on the live web, and a sandbox that allows for secure playback of plugin-enabled content - all of which are open-source software.

item.title: Guitars of the USSR and the Jolana Special in Azerbaijani Music
item.description:
Throughout the whole performance he does amazing things with trills and mimics vocal ornamentation by using bends with the left hand along with bends with the whammy bar. This kind of virtuosic performance would of been impossible using a Tonika or Orpheus guitar. This guitar is everywhere: Here is a great post from a fellow.

Top 2 Comments:

dsign:

Jesus those things are big!

> It was unreasonably heavy and made of cheap wood, with a neck like a carved baseball bat.

Guitar necks need to withstand the tension of the strings, and any Russian-educated engineer tasked by the politburo with making a guitar out of fiberboard[^2], will plug tension plus safety margins into the secant formula[^1] and immediately realize that some steel rods from Magnitogorsk for reinforcement are in order, and promptly discover that they only have 1/2'' ones. Oh well.

[^1]: http://www.engineeringcorecourses.com/solidmechanics2/C5-buc...

[^2]: Not that there's anything wrong with fiberboard for guitars; see Danelectro. In fact, if you own a laser cutter and want to make something cool with it, an electric guitar is a great project.

SubGenius:

I discovered Rəhman Məmmədli on this KEXP video a while back. Very mesmerizing trio. I've been playing guitars of all kinds and all styles for years but have never really heard anything like this - the guitar itself seems to be heavily modded for the microtonal/vibrato style playing - but it's not just the guitar, a lot of the technique is in his hands.

He's playing a Jolana guitar here.

It's beautiful. I especially love the last song Qarabag Atlari.

The rest of the band is pretty good too. A very minimal guitar + keys + perc trio that allows for very unique sonic and open compositions.

Being a guitar nerd, it was nice to find something recent that completely blew me away. I definitely need to check out more Azerbaijani guitarists.

I'm not sure how I'd describe his style - it reminds me of a more primal/raw/exciting version of Jeff Beck. Not to compare obviously, this guy is brilliant and stands on his own.
